english: Like the opportunity of a lifetime sits, right here. Right now.
In this here weird cave lake.
There is SOMETHING in the water.
It takes shape. A figure. Fluid and shimmering.
One of the old guardians of the deep places.
The voice comes from everywhere. From the water itself.
My domain is what you stand in- what you drink and bathe and boil...
Are you going to attack me?
(Raise your fists.) "I will FIGHT you, lake!"
These here waters, flowing through time and space.
No beast am I nor blade of passion.
A thing-of-passion, to crave a violence...
Not. Not now, as the tides foretell.
You swing a HARD FIST against the surface of the water.
The water seems to ripple back towards you.
The fist of the iron man is not fast enough to hit the crucial part.
No harm was done. No harm will return.
Snell stands upon the shore, arms crossed.
The land-rights to this cavern. Yours. To do with as you please.
This cave. Its pool. The shore.
All yours, for the low, low, low price of twenty-five-thousand shiny crowns.
That's one hell of an offer. Let's hear this Lake-Thing out.
You do have that fortune from the Deck...
With a hint of potential return.
Your companion says, loudly across the cavern, "That'd be a good price- if this was a developed region."
What if it becomes a developed region in the future, then?
Then they'd call you investor-cleric, lord of the futures.
And I also offer healing water.
Don't go drinking random elementals in cavern lakes.
That's how you catch esoteric pneumonia.
Though you can easily die from many other dungeon-diseases.
The waters stir as you approach.
What do land-rights even mean down here?
Why would I want to own a lake?
Twenty-five thousand? That's absurd. Surely we can negotiate.
What else can you tell me about this place?
How long have you been here?
The many coins sink into the depths of the lake.
The many, many coins sink into the depths of the lake.
The elemental swirls with satisfaction, and a piece of paper floats to the surface.
It is done. These waters... this land... yours.
May you find what you seek in the deep places.
Sweet. Good way to spend your vast fortune.
If you get some stairs put in- make sure it's populated enough for the City Below to not swallow it or shift it around...
Give or take five to fifteen years, and you'll be a big time land-owning over-class type person.
I feel like I might regret this in a couple of years.
Of course, Lord cleric. Of course.
The elemental in the water slowly ripples out, fading off into the crevices of the cave.
E-Guess that's it. (Look at your wet piece of paper.)
Official ownership. Recognized by the old laws.
No goblin. No dwarf. No cleric. May claim what is yours.
Privacy. Prestige. A place to call your own.
The surface-dwellers covet such things, do they not?
Very well. Ten thousand crowns. My final offer.
The price is the price, surface-walker.
A small sphere of water rises to meet you.
It tastes like cave. With a hint of algae.
Insane behavior, Snell whispers to himself on the shore. "Absolutely insane."
These caverns are old. Older than your cities.
Many have walked these paths. Few have returned.
The deep places keep their secrets.
Cryptic. As expected from an elemental.
I flow. I wait. I remain.
Since before the dwarves. Since before the cats.
Simply another elemental left behind by some esoteric event.
